title: Nonlocal-nonlinear phonon polaritons
authors: Gonzalo Álvarez-Pérez, Line Jelver, Alexander Paarmann, Simone De Liberato
abstract: When light is confined to deeply subwavelength volumes, optical responses can become nonlocal. Yet how nonlocality reshapes nonlinear light-matter interactions remains largely unexplored, particularly in dielectrics. Here, we theoretically uncover a new class of nonlinear optical processes arising from the interplay between optical-phonon propagation and ionic-bond anharmonicity in polar crystals. We show that, unlike conventional local nonlinearities, this mechanism enables second-order responses even in centrosymmetric materials. Moreover, these responses can be tuned by the confinement and resonantly enhanced near optical-phonon resonances. Using density functional perturbation theory, we quantify the resulting nonlocal second-order susceptibilities in representative polar crystals. Our results establish nonlocal-nonlinear optics as a new regime of light-matter interaction in dielectrics.
summary: This paper develops a theory to study nonlocal nonlinear optics in polar crystals by examining the coupling between light and lattice vibrations (phonon polaritons). It reveals a novel second-order nonlinear process stemming from lattice anharmonicity that can generate strong SHG signals even in materials that are otherwise centrosymmetric. The findings establish a new theoretical regime for light-matter interaction in dielectrics.
main_problem: To theoretically investigate how nonlocality, arising from phonon confinement, reshapes nonlinear light-matter interactions in dielectrics, particularly in polar crystals.
main_result: The study identifies a new, nonlocal second-order nonlinear mechanism enabled by the interplay between optical-phonon propagation and ionic-bond anharmonicity, which can dominate SHG even in centrosymmetric materials.
method: The authors use Density Functional Perturbation Theory (DFPT) to quantify the nonlocal second-order susceptibilities by analyzing the anharmonic potential energy functional.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using polar crystals exhibiting phonon polaritons (PhPs). The nonlinearity is derived from the anharmonic terms ($U_3$) in the lattice potential, which are expanded in terms of wavevectors ($k, k'$).
key_observables: Nonlocal second-order susceptibilities ($\chi^{(2)}$), Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG) signals.
important_parameters: Phonon polariton resonance frequencies, wavevector dependence ($k$), and the degree of confinement (deeply subwavelength volumes).
main_assumptions: The theory assumes the potential energy $U$ depends only on lattice displacement, confining nonlocality and anharmonicity to lattice origins.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares local and nonlocal $\chi^{(2)}$ across the Reststrahlen Band for various crystals. Figure 2 compares the local versus nonlocal origins of the nonlinearity.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (nonlocal nonlinearity in dielectrics), develops the theoretical framework using lattice dynamics and anharmonic potentials, calculates the nonlocal susceptibilities using DFPT, and presents results showing the new nonlinear regime.
why_interesting: This work bridges condensed matter theory (lattice dynamics, DFPT) with quantum optics (polaritons, nonlinear light-matter interaction), providing a detailed theoretical mechanism for enhanced nonlinear optical responses in solid-state dielectrics.

(a) In the local picture (left), the lattice response is identical from one unit cell to the next, so the second-order polarization at frequency ω2 is determined solely by the local response to the incident field at ω1. In the nonlocal picture (right), the lattice response varies across neighboring unit cells, giving rise to a spatially-dispersive (nonlocal) second-order polarization.
